title: Sparse Sum-of-Squares Layers for Certified Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.34590v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A central limitation of modern machine learning systems is the lack of formal certificates guaranteeing their behavior beyond empirical, sample-based evaluation. Sum-of-squares (SOS) methods provide such guarantees by certifying polynomial inequalities over continuous domains via semidefinite programming (SDP). While prior work has introduced SDP layers as differentiable components in neural networks, repeated learning calls can lose the computational benefit of the forward program's sparse representation. We propose Sparse SOS Layers, differentiable value layers whose backward passes reuse the local coordinates of the forward solve. Under a fixed template and learned objective coefficients, each layer avoids building dense certificates and reuses its sparse structure across training steps. translated_title: 用于可认证学习的稀疏平方和层
translated_abstract: 现代机器学习系统的一个核心局限性在于，除了经验性的、基于样本的评估之外，缺乏能够保证其行为的形式化证书。平方和（SOS）方法通过半定规划（SDP）在连续域上认证多项式不等式，从而提供此类保证。虽然先前的工作已将SDP层作为可微分组件引入神经网络，但反复的学习调用可能会丧失前向程序稀疏表示的计算优势。我们提出了稀疏SOS层，这是一种可微分价值层，其反向传播过程可复用前向求解的局部坐标。在固定模板和学习的目标系数下，每一层都避免了构建稠密证书，并在训练步骤中复用其稀疏结构。与现有方法相比，我们的方法在总热调用时间上实现了高达2.7倍的加速，内存使用量降低了近100倍（1.7……
tldr: 提出稀疏SOS层——一种可微分价值层，通过在反向传播中复用前向SDP求解的稀疏局部坐标来避免构建稠密证书，实现最高2.7倍加速和近100倍的内存降低，从而为机器学习系统提供形式化认证保证。
en_tdlr: Sparse SOS Layers are differentiable value layers whose backward passes reuse the sparse local coordinates of the forward SDP solve, avoiding dense certificates and achieving up to 2.7x speedup with nearly 100x lower memory usage for certified learning.
